display.title: Episode 504: The Sly Fox and the Cheese (Yud-Tes Kislev)
display.summary_short: A Yud-Tes Kislev show: the Alter Rebbe and the soul of the Torah, Shema with a first-grade class, and the fox in the well, a fable about the tricks of the yetzer hara.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Yud-Tes Kislev itself. Uncle Yossi explains why the day is celebrated: the Alter Rebbe was freed from prison and his life spared by a miracle. The Torah is like a person, with a body (its letters and words) and a soul (its inner, hidden meaning), and the Alter Rebbe taught both, writing the Shulchan Aruch HaRav and the Tanya; Moshiach will teach the innermost secrets of the Torah to all. On this day we make resolutions to learn more Torah and do more mitzvos. After the Hakochainik march, a first-grade class from a Boro Park girls' school recites the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time: a hungry fox sees 'cheese' at the bottom of a well, rides a bucket down and finds only water and the moon's reflection. Stuck, he sings happily until a second fox comes by, tricks him into riding the other bucket down, and escapes, telling him to play the same trick on the next fox. The lesson: the yetzer hara is that tricky, and a Tzivos Hashem soldier fights it with Torah, davening and daily tzedakah, giving extra before Shabbos candles. The show ends with candle-lighting times.
display.lesson: The yetzer hara is full of tricks; fight it with Torah, sincere davening and tzedakah every day.

date.note: 'Today, Yud-Tes Kislev'; 19 Kislev 5752 fell on Tuesday 26 Nov 1991, the show's night. Candles 4:12 fit.

advisories.note: The Alter Rebbe's imprisonment and release are mentioned briefly.

privacy.note: The visiting class's teacher is named on air; no children are named.

sources_cited.note: 'Zos haTorah adam': the Torah is compared to a person, with body and soul.
